study_identification_part.si_4_title: Developmental trajectories of neuroanatomical alterations associated with the 16p11.2 Copy Number Variations

answer: NIHPD normative developmental dataset (339 children, 874 scans; ages 4.5–18.5 years)
16p11.2 CNV cohort from European consortium and Simons VIP (56 deletion carriers, 19 duplication carriers, 105 controls aged 4.5–23 years)
dc_1_datasets_using_in_this_study.detail: Longitudinal NIHPD data provide the normative growth model; the 16p11.2 deletion/duplication cohort (with site-matched controls) constitutes the study dataset.

"This included 56 16p11.2 BP4-5 deletion carriers ... 19 duplication carriers ... and 105 controls ... ages ranging from 4.5 and 23 years."

answer: NIHPD normative dataset: Normative training dataset to model age- and sex-dependent brain growth trajectories.
16p11.2 CNV cohort: Clinical study cohort (deletion, duplication, and controls) normalized against the NIHPD-based trajectories; controls also used to adjust for scanner/protocol effects.
dc_2_purpose_of_each_dataset.detail: NIHPD supplies the reference curves; 16p11.2 cohort (patients and controls) are scored against the norm and include control data to align scanning protocols.
dc_2_purpose_of_each_dataset.supporting_text: "As normative reference data for brain growth, we used the multi-site longitudinal data from ... NIHPD." ... "We only included participants between 4.5 and 23 years of age... 56 deletion carriers ... 19 duplication carriers, and 105 controls." ... "We estimated a linear model ... on the Z-scored segmented volumes and the voxel-wise ... of the 16p11.2 control data" to adjust protocol differences.
